estatePlan.concept: A $15 million Saint Lucian cliffside estate composed as a low-slung tropical-modern villa and a discreet guest pavilion, arranged around an elevated infinity pool terrace oriented to northern Caribbean views. The architecture uses deep shade, pale mineral walls, volcanic stone, warm timber and dark bronze framing to give a refined, climate-responsive character.
estatePlan.character: Contemporary Caribbean resort architecture with strong horizontal rooflines, sheltered indoor-outdoor rooms, carefully controlled arrival privacy, expansive north-facing glazing and substantial shaded exterior living. The main villa is the primary view-facing residence; the smaller pavilion offers independent guest privacy without competing with the principal mass.

requirements.statement: Design an extraordinary luxury estate in Saint Lucia with a construction and estate-design target of $15 million.
The estate shall respond to Saint Lucia through a climate-responsive, view-oriented Caribbean luxury architectural character.
North-facing principal rooms, terraces and pool are reserved for ocean and sunset outlook while the south side handles private arrival.
requirements.value: North view axis and south arrival separation

program.role: Primary owner residence with formal entertaining, chef service spaces and two private bedroom suites.
Independent one-bedroom guest accommodation with lounge, dressing and private terrace.
Ocean-oriented terrace, infinity pool and private tropical garden landscape.

zones.purpose: Secure south-side vehicle arrival, turning and formal approach to the main residence.
Protected north-side outdoor living zone for dining, lounging, swimming and Caribbean views.
Quiet east-side guest compound buffered by lawn and planted garden reserve.

architecture.intent: A long, disciplined two-storey horizontal bar frames the northern ocean outlook and creates deep shaded edges.
A compact single-storey stone pavilion remains subordinate to the primary residence and opens toward its own garden terrace.

relationships.intent: The main villa directly addresses the ocean-view terrace through full-height north glazing.
The outdoor living terrace supports and visually extends to the infinity pool.
The guest pavilion is paired with an independent terrace and planted privacy reserve.
The formal south arrival court connects the site gate with the principal entry.

considerations.intent: Keep northern facades visually open to Caribbean views; pool and terrace remain lower than the villa roofline.
South-side arrival glazing is controlled and the guest pavilion is offset eastward to preserve owner privacy.
Maintain a generous unbuilt northern outdoor room between residence, terrace and pool.
The garden reserve creates a soft private landscape setting for the guest accommodation.

circulation.purpose: Private vehicular arrival from the south gate to the covered main-residence entry.
Pedestrian route from the main arrival entry to the independent guest pavilion.
Protected pedestrian connection from the arrival side of the residence around the western garden edge to the ocean-view terrace.
Direct pedestrian approach from the principal outdoor terrace to the infinity pool.
